newsitem.title: USA: Ford to idle two plants next week.
newsitem.headline: Ford to idle two plants next week.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Thursday a parts shortage has forced it to suspend operations next week at its small car plants in Kansas City, Mo., and Hermosillo, Mexico, next week.
About 3,600 hourly workers are affected by the idling of the Kansas City plant, which makes about 4,500 Contours and Mystiques a week.
Ford said about 2,300 hourly workers will be idled at the Hermosillo plant, where weekly output of Escorts and Tracers is normally about 3,500 units.

Ford said it has scheduled daily overtime this week at the following truck plants: Edison, N.J.; Kansas City; Loraine, Ohio; Kentucky Truck in Louisville, Ky.; Norfolk, Va.; St. Paul, Minn.; and St. Louis.

General Motors Corp. said it has scheduled overtime for the week of July 21 at its Janesville, Wis., sport utility plant, the Oshawa, Ont., full-size pickup truck plant, and the minivan plant in Doraville, Ga.
Chrysler Corp. said it plans overtime next week at its Jefferson-North Jeep plant in Detroit. Plants in Newark, Del., and Sterling Heights, Mich., will not operate due to model changeover.
In Canada, overtime will be run at the Windsor Assembly minivan plant, the Pillette full-size van facility, and the Bramalea plant that produces LH cars.
